verdict.summary: Issue #216 is a valid, current target, but its contract remains too ambiguous and unverifiable for implementation. It does not define the metadata boundary, documentation dispositions, inherited dependency scope, objective acceptance evidence, failure behavior, or rollout decisions.

blockingFindings.title: Package-metadata authority and layering are undefined
blockingFindings.details: The requirement for “one authoritative package.json surface” does not identify the authoritative file, enumerate fields owned at the root versus package level, define permitted package-local metadata, or specify how conflicting values are resolved. A worker cannot determine the intended end state without making semantic owner decisions.

blockingFindings.title: Documentation scope and disposition are not specified
blockingFindings.details: The issue provides no inventory of affected root or package documents, no per-document keep, relocate, redirect, retire, or remove disposition, and no exact PRD.md/PLAN.md precedence wording. Deciding which documents compete with authority or may be removed is ambiguous and potentially destructive.

blockingFindings.title: Dependency and residual-scope claims are unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The contract depends on work attributed to #179 and claims to replace #178, but it identifies no verified #179 revision or delivered-state evidence and does not map every #178 requirement to completed, retained, or residual scope. The available state therefore cannot establish prerequisites, prevent omissions, or rule out duplicated work.

blockingFindings.title: Single-lane ownership and boundaries are unclear
blockingFindings.details: “PLAN lane 2” does not define the lane owner, the exact files or repository surfaces it owns, or its boundary against repository-authority, package-layout, validation, and documentation work. The contract cannot safely assign one implementation lane or adjudicate overlaps.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance criteria are subjective and not evidentiary
blockingFindings.details: Terms such as “internally consistent,” “remaining root documentation,” and “no stale competing authority” are not expressed as objective assertions over named files, metadata fields, references, or repository searches. The issue also does not state what reviewable evidence proves each acceptance condition.

blockingFindings.title: Failure, compatibility, migration, and rollout behavior are missing
blockingFindings.details: The issue does not say how to fail closed when metadata or document authority is ambiguous, whether package consumers or published artifacts require compatibility handling, how moved or retired documentation remains discoverable, or how the consolidation is rolled out and reverted. These choices must be resolved before implementation.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner decision required: define the authoritative metadata surface, root-owned and package-owned fields, layering rules, and conflict resolution.
Owner decision required: approve an affected-document inventory, a disposition for each document, and exact PRD.md/PLAN.md precedence language.
Owner decision required: identify the verified #179 prerequisite revision and map all #178 requirements to delivered or residual scope.
Owner decision required: define the implementation lane owner and its file and responsibility boundaries.
Owner decision required: approve objective end-state assertions, required review evidence, fail-closed behavior, compatibility or migration handling, and rollout strategy.
The independent exact-head Validate gate owns execution of git diff --check and git submodule status --recursive; their intentionally absent results are not findings in this review.
